product_one_liner.value: Together AI provides AI engineers and researchers a production cloud platform to run inference, fine-tune and train AI models, and access GPU clusters.
product_one_liner.notes: Together AI describes its GPU cloud as purpose-built for AI engineers and researchers and its platform as supporting model building, fine-tuning, deployment, inference, and GPU clusters.

pricing_page.notes: Together AI has a public pricing page describing pricing for its products.

named_customers.notes: named_customers: The Trust Center customer statement explicitly names Salesforce and Zoom as customers. | named_customers.0: The Trust Center names Salesforce as one of Together AI’s customers. | named_customers.1: The Trust Center names Zoom as one of Together AI’s customers.

employee_band.notes: LinkedIn displays 440 employees, which falls in the requested 201-500 band.

hq_location.notes: hq_city: The LinkedIn company profile directly identifies San Francisco as Together AI headquarters. | hq_country: The LinkedIn company profile identifies Together AI headquarters as San Francisco, California, and gives a US headquarters address.

founded_year.notes: The company homepage states a foundingDate of 2022.

eng_blog.notes: The Research Blog index describes engineering insights and lists multiple technical posts; the cited posts discuss inference benchmarking, compiler optimization, kernels, and production inference infrastructure.

public_docs.notes: The public documentation site offers multiple developer guides, including running models, fine-tuning, and GPU cluster documentation.

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: A live Greenhouse application is for Machine Learning Engineer - Inference and includes an Apply control, so an AI/ML role is open.

model_provider.value: Together AI does not identify one exclusive provider: it offers models from providers such as DeepSeek, Qwen, and Mistral; third-party models hosted on Together run on its infrastructure, while optional passthrough models can forward prompts to upstream providers.
model_provider.notes: Together documentation describes third-party models from providers including DeepSeek, Qwen, and Mistral, and says hosted third-party models run on Together infrastructure; it also describes optional passthrough to upstream providers. This supports a multi-provider answer rather than one exclusive provider.
